texts.preamble: Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Kabc020288742022 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore. (Scch-9) Dated This The 8th Day Of July 2025 Present Smt.Nirmala.M.C.,B.Com.,L.L.B ., Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Acjm Mvc No.5262/2022 Petitioner: Sri. Venkatanarayana Rao, S/o. Late K Gipinath Rao, Aged about 50 years, Residing at: Kadirenahalli Village, Thokalahalli, Gowribidanur Taluk, Chikkaballapur District. (By Sri. K.V.Vijayakumar Gowda - Adv.) V/s. Respondents: 1. Shanthakumar.M.N, S/o. Adinarayanappa, Mallenahalli village, Gowribidanur Taluk, Chikkaballapur District - 561208. (Owner of the Auto Rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975) (By Sri. Basavaraju.L - Adv.) (Scch-9) 2 MVC.No.5262/2022 2. Shriram General Insurance Co., Ltd., No.3/5, 3rd Floor, Sv Arcade, Belekahalli main road, Bannarughatta road, Iim-B Post, Bangalore - 560 076. (Policy No.10003/31/17/629400 valid from 07.03.2017 to 06.03.2018) (By Sri.M.E.Madhu Sudhan - Adv.) Judgment
texts.facts: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident. 2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under: On 24.02,2018 at about 03.30 pm. When the petitioner was travelling in Auto rickshaw bg No.KA-40-A- 3975 along with other passengers on Gowribidanur towards vatada Hosahalli, in between Nakkhalli gate and Narasapura gate and on reaching near Eco Home (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5262/2022 Asharama, Chikkaballapur District sustained grievous injuries as the driver of said Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA- 40-A-3975 driven the same in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed without following traffic rules dashed against the repaired auto rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-40- A-405l on left side of the road and caused accident & injuries to petitioner. The accident occurred due to sole rash & negligent driving of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 by its driver. After the accident petitioner took treatment for one month at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was working as a Cooking Bhattas and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month. Due to accidental injuries sustained by him he is unable to continue his avocation as earlier. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 by its driver. The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally are liable (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.5262/2022 to pay the compensation to the petitioner. 3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.2 have appeared through their respective counsel and respondent No.2 has filed its objections to the main petition. 4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts of the same. Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the offending Auto regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act. It has contented that, at the time of accident, the driver of the offending Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 does not posses valid and effective driving licence to drive the same. It has contended that, the offending Auto (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.5262/2022 bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 in question did not hold valid permit and FC as on the date of accident. It has denied the issuance of the policy in respect of Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975. Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 in the alleged accident. Further contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself as the petitioner was negligently going in the vehicle which was filled with above the seating capacity and Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117687756/ 2 as such the vehicle lost control at the material time of the accident and contributed the accident. The entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner to cause the accident. Further contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful. With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1, one Medical Record Technician at Victoria Hospital has examined as PW.2 and Dr.S.Ramachandra has examined as PW.3 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.13. On the other hand, RTO, Chikkaballapura has examined as RW.1 and Legal Manager, Shri Ram GIC Ltd., has examined as RW.2 and in all got marked Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed their side evidence. (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.5262/2022 7. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 24.02,2018 at about 03.30 pm. When he was travelling in Auto rickshaw bg No.KA-40-A-3975 along with other passengers on Gowribidanur towards vatada Hosahalli, in between Nakkhalli gate and Narasapura gate and on reaching near Eco Home Asharama, Chikkaballapur District sustained grievous injuries as the driver of said (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.5262/2022 Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 driven the same in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed without following traffic rules dashed against the repaired auto rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-405l on left side of the road. Due to said impact he sustained grievous injuries. 10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition. He also got marked Ex.P1 to P8 which are FIR, complaint, IMV report, spot panchanama, charge sheet, wound certificate, OPD slip and 2 X-rays.
texts.arguments: It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343. Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under: 12,500 x 12 x 11 x 15% = Rs.2,47,500/- Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117687756/ 6 Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.2,47,500/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity. f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities: The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable do his day to day activities as earlier. The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the citation reported in: a) (2018) 7 Supreme Court Cases 558 (Amrit Paul (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.5262/2022 Singh and another Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co., Ltd., and others) where in it is held that: " A. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss.149(2), (1), 66(1), (3), 2(28), (31), (47) and 166 - Defences available to insurer - Use of motor vehicle as a transport vehicle in public place without permit - Prohibition under S.66(1) of MV Act, 1988 with respect to - Invocation of - Offending truck on date of accident not having the permit as required under S.66(1) of MV Act - Exceptions to S.66(1) as given under S.66(3) of MV Act - Applicability of - Prerequisites as to - Having regard to S. 66(1) of MV Act, 1988 which prescribes that no owner of a motor vehicle shall use or permit the use of the vehicle as a transport vehicle in any public place whether or not such vehicle is actually carrying any passengers or goods save in accordance with the conditions of a permit granted or countersigned by a Regional or State Transport Authority or any prescribed authority, held, use of a vehicle as a transport vehicle in public place Though S. 66(3) of (SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.5262/2022 without a permit is a fundamental statutory infraction MV Act, 1988 carves out certain exceptions to S. 66(1), in order to invoke those exceptions the same must be pleaded and proved- In present case, no material brought on record by owner of offending vehicle (i.e. insured) Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117687756/ 8 to prove that he was having a permit of offending vehicle on date of However, order accident - Hence held, insurer not liable in such a case passed by courts below in such a situation directing insurer to pay compensation amount to claimants with interest with the stipulation that insurer must be entitled to recover the same from owner and driver of vehicle, held, was proper, being in consonance with principle of pay and recover - Words and Phrases Vehicle", "motor vehicle, "transport vehicle", "permit", "articulated vehicle." Further it is also held that:- 9. The relevant part of sub- section (3) is extracted below: " 66. (3) The provisions of sub- section (1) shall not apply-- (a) to any transport vehicle owned by the Central Government or a State Government and used for Government purposes unconnected with any commercial enterprise; (b) to any transport vehicle owned by a local authority or by a person acting under contract with a local authority and used solely for road cleansing, road watering or conservancy purposes; (c) to any transport vehicle used solely for police, fire brigade or ambulance purposes; (d) to any transport vehicle used solely for the conveyance of corpses and the mourners accompanying the corpses; (SCCH-9) 24 MVC.No.5262/2022 (e) to any transport vehicle used for to wing adisabled vehicle or for removing goo ds from a disabled vehicle to a place of safety; (f) to any transport vehicle used for any other public purpose as may be prescribed by the State Government in this behalf; (g) to any transport vehicle used by a person who manufactures or deal in or deals in motor vehicles or builds bodies for attachment to chassis, solely for such purposes and in accordance Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117687756/ 9 with such conditions as Central Government may, by notification in Official Gazette, specify in this behalf; (h) x x x x (i) to any goods vehicle, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 3,000 kilograms." b) In (2018) 8 Supreme Court Cases 492 (Rani and others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others) wherein it is held that: (SCCH-9) 25 MVC.No.5262/2022 " - Defence raised by insurer that offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit to operate in the State concerned - Accepting that defence, High Court absolving the insurer and fastening the liability on the insured i.e., the owner of offending vehicle directing him to satisfy the award - Held, even in such a case, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle - Order of High Court modified accordingly". c) In MFA No.101342/2017 (Shri Basavaraj Vs. Mr.K.M.Altaf Hussain and another) wherein it is held at para No.14 that: " ... the judgment and award insofar as fastening liability on the owner of bus is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and it is set-aside holding that the insurance company shall indemnify the owner of the bus by paying compensation to the claimants". (SCCH-9) 26 MVC.No.5262/2022 and same point is considered in the citation reported 2018 ACJ 1768 (Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. Tata AIG General Ins. Co., Ltd., and others) wherein it is held that: " Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 149(2)(a)(i)(c) read with section 66 - Motor Insurance - Permit - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order - Tribunal found that offending truck was being plied without valid permit and directed insurance company to pay and recover - Order of the tribunal was confirmed by the High Court - Onus lies on the insured to prove possession of permit - No evidence produced by insured to prove that he had a permit to ply the vehicle on the date of accident - Use of transport vehicle in a public place without a permit is a fundamental statutory infraction - Whether the High Court and Tribunal were justified in directing the insurance company to pay compensation amount and then Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117687756/ 10 recover the same from owner and driver - Held: yes". also in the citation reported in 2020 ACJ 2560 (New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and another) wherein it is held that: " Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Section 149(2)(a) and (b) read with section 149 (a), 149 (4) and 149(7) - Motor Insurance - Act or comprehensive policy - Breach of - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover (SCCH-9) 27 MVC.No.5262/2022 order - In a case where insurance company successfully establishes that insured had committed breach of policy as per section 149 (2) (a) and breach was fundamental contributing to the cause of accident or policy is void as per section 149(2)(b), whether in view of the mandate under section 149(1) insurance company would be liable to satisfy the award vis-a-vis third party and entitled to recover the amount from the insured - Held: yes; however if court comes to a finding that third party has played fraud or was in collusion with the insured for wrongful gain to themselves then court may exercise its discretion not to fasten liability on insurance company".
